correctness.rationale: A surviving vertex of a unit equilateral face covers its whole closed face; if all three are deleted, only its three opposite edge-neighbor centers may cover interior. Each surviving opposite site removes an independent nonoverlapping cap of area pi/6-sqrt(3)/4 with one circular boundary arc of length pi/3. Summing faces gives area aF-cB and length (pi/3)B. I.i.d. deletion gives face q^3 and exposed edge q^3(1-q), with finite-range ergodicity and O(R) window error for area and length density. Independently checked one/two-face cases and the q polynomials at eleven q values.

The all-q stochastic density follows with a sharp geometry-specific coefficient and predicts nonadditivity of adjacent failures.
